quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It makes you feel overly confident.
It makes it harder to think clearly.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your coordination and balance, and makes it hard to judge distances and react quickly.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at other cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down, turn on your hazard flashers and carefully leave the road. Park as far off the road as possible so other drivers can see you. Open your hood to show your car is disabled.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:
questions.explanation: You must always let a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog cross first. They have the right-of-way.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that an upcoming bridge is narrow. You may not have room to pass a truck. Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that a T intersection is ahead. Be ready to turn right or left and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for vehicles crossing your path.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and turn around to reach the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and turn around to reach the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: Road rage can be reduced by:

options.text: Leaving extra time to get where you are going.

questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and leave plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors to see traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, look over your shoulder to spot any vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers may keep you awake, but they do not lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention leads to collisions. Following too closely causes most rear-end crashes.

questions.question: A driver going much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let other cars pass.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be unsafe. On a two-lane road, pull over if traffic backs up behind you. Only drive slowly if road conditions require it.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Turns off the seat belt warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with a fist width between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from the curb.

questions.question: After an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at or near the scene.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Stay out of traffic lanes so another vehicle does not hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Increase the risk of skidding on wet roads.

questions.explanation: Worn tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. They also increase the risk of skidding on wet roads.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. Move into the left lane before the intersection. Wait for the path to be clear before turning.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and do not follow them too closely.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but move out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: If a driver is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Look at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Speeding up may anger them and make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther back from the vehicle in front of you.
Drive carefully around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Leave extra distance between your vehicle and others because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
See what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Not exchange information with other drivers.
Tell the other driver you are not responsible.
Let the other driver report the accident.

questions.explanation: Exchange names, addresses, driver license numbers, vehicle details (license plate, make, model, year), and insurance information with all other drivers involved.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol effect may get weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink mixed with a cold medicine can affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Pull to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. In heavy traffic, move slowly to the side when you can.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the road ahead has curves. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: Where is passing not allowed?
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass other vehicles on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also makes it harder to judge speed and distance. Alcohol lowers your inhibitions and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and could crash into it.
